models.description: Measured here: 100% structurally valid actions, 62% expected action, 189 ms median. The fastest of the three and the one to reach for when a character must answer within a beat. Pairs with the Model_Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M preset.

Measured here: 100% structurally valid actions, 81% expected action, 278 ms median. The best quality per millisecond of the three for reactive characters, and the model behind the recorded sample runs. Pairs with the Model_Granite-4.1-3B-Q4_K_M preset.

Measured here: 100% structurally valid actions, 94% expected action in the Deliberative profile, 574 ms median. The most accurate of the three and the only one measured to clearly benefit from deliberation; suits directors and planners on a slow tick. Pairs with the Model_Qwen3.5-4B-Q4_K_M preset.

Measured here on 262 situations recorded in the sample scenes: 79% expected action with Max Memory Entries set to 1 on the decision maker config (72% with full memory; it repeats what its memory lists), at a 191 ms median and 2.2 GB, against 72% and 552 ms for Qwen3.5 4B. The fastest accurate option for many characters: 160 decisions per minute with eight in PrisonYard. Needs a llama-server newer than b11429 (support merged 2026-10-07). LFM Open License v1.0: free below USD 10M annual revenue, check it before shipping.

Measured here on 262 situations recorded in the sample scenes: 79% expected action at a 436 ms median, against 72% for Qwen3.5 4B. Qwen3.5-4B-Base read once with a pointer head over the options. Apache-2.0. Same base as Qwen3.5 4B above, which makes it the like-for-like comparison. Causal, so the server shares the work of reading one situation between several questions.

Measured here on 262 situations recorded in the sample scenes: 86% expected action, the most accurate model tested in either paradigm (Qwen3.5 4B: 72%), at a 735 ms median and 5.6 GB. Too slow for many characters on one 8 GB card (2.2 s median with eight in PrisonYard); suits a few important characters or a director. A community quantisation of jaredpalmer/kev-9b by turintech, Apache-2.0.

Measured here: 54% expected action on 262 situations recorded in the sample scenes, at 73 ms. Too weak for character decisions in this project's tests. A small encoder decision model (ModernBERT, 0.42B), Apache-2.0. Its file sets a temperature of 0.1 for questions of 11 or more options, so it reports near-certain probabilities whether or not it is right. An encoder reads the whole prompt at once, so it shares no work between questions and long situations must fit one batch.

Measured here: 45% expected action on 262 situations recorded in the sample scenes, at 30 ms; too weak for character decisions. The smallest decision model listed here: a 0.14B ModernBERT encoder, Apache-2.0, 168 MB. llama-server loads it as the same decision type as Laya, with the same limits.
